subject: ss-medical-oncology
title: Gastrointestinal stromal tumour: KIT and PDGFRA genomics, risk stratification, imatinib therapy and resistance management

steps.tx: Gastrointestinal stromal tumours GIST represent the most common mesenchymal neoplasms of the digestive tract, arising from pacemaker **interstitial cells of Cajal**. Diagnosis is confirmed by uniform immunohistochemical positivity for receptor tyrosine kinase **KIT CD117** and **DOG1** anoctamin-1. True GIST tumours must be carefully distinguished histologically from smooth muscle leiomyomas, schwannomas, and solitary fibrous tumours.

steps.tx: The field shows spindle cell **GIST** fascicles with diffuse brown **KIT CD117** staining of membranes and cytoplasm plus **DOG1** positivity in the inset. This paired pattern confirms origin from interstitial cells of Cajal. Recognizing both markers matters because true GIST must be separated from leiomyoma and schwannoma, and KIT positivity points toward tyrosine kinase inhibitor therapy.
steps.say: This micrograph shows gastric spindle cell GIST fascicles with strong diffuse KIT staining of cell membranes and cytoplasm, with DOG1 coexpression in the inset. The lesson defines GIST as arising from pacemaker interstitial cells of Cajal and confirmed by these two markers. This pattern distinguishes GIST from smooth muscle or nerve sheath tumors and supports targeted inhibitor treatment.

steps.tx: Activating **KIT exon 11** mutations involving in-frame deletions or point substitutions within the juxtamembrane domain represent the primary driver alteration in approximately 70% of GISTs. Tumours harbouring exon 11 mutations exhibit exquisite sensitivity to the competitive tyrosine kinase inhibitor **imatinib** mesylate at standard doses of 400 mg daily, achieving objective response rates exceeding 80%.

steps.tx: In contrast, activating **PDGFRA exon 18 D842V** point mutations confer primary intrinsic resistance to imatinib, sunitinib, and regorafenib. In the landmark phase I/II **NAVIGATOR trial**, the selective type I kinase inhibitor **avapritinib** produced an unprecedented 95% objective response rate in advanced D842V-mutant GIST, establishing avapritinib as the undisputed targeted standard of care for this unique genomic subset.

steps.tx: In completely resected primary GIST exhibiting high-risk features, the landmark randomized phase III **SSGXVIII/AIO trial** proved that **adjuvant imatinib** for 3 years significantly improves both recurrence-free survival and overall survival compared to 1 year of treatment. Five-year overall survival rose from 82% with 1 year of imatinib to 92% with 3 years, establishing 36 months as the global standard.

steps.tx: For patients developing secondary resistance or intolerance to imatinib, the oral multi-targeted tyrosine kinase inhibitor **Sunitinib** represents the established second-line standard of care. Sunitinib inhibits KIT, PDGFRA, and VEGFR receptors, demonstrating substantial clinical benefit against secondary mutations within the ATP-binding pocket encoded by KIT exons 13 and 14.
steps.say: For patients developing secondary resistance or intolerance to imatinib, the oral multi-targeted tyrosine kinase inhibitor Sunitinib represents the established second-line standard of care. Sunitinib inhibits KIT, PDGFRA, and VEGFR receptors, demonstrating substantial clinical benefit against secondary mutations within the ATP-binding pocket encoded by KIT exons 13 and 14.

steps.tx: Approved as fourth-line therapy in the pivotal **INVICTUS trial**, **Ripretinib** is a novel dual switch-pocket kinase inhibitor. Ripretinib binds both the kinase switch pocket and activation loop, locking the receptor in an inactive conformation. In advanced GIST refractory to imatinib, sunitinib, and regorafenib, ripretinib significantly prolonged progression-free survival while demonstrating a favourable safety profile.

steps.tx: Risk stratification in localized GIST utilizes the **modified NIH consensus criteria** or Armed Forces Institute of Pathology Miettinen tables. Recurrence risk is calculated from three primary parameters: anatomical tumour site, tumour size, and **mitotic rate** per 5 mm2 or 50 high-power fields. Gastric GISTs produce substantially lower malignant potential than small bowel or rectal tumours of identical size and mitotic index.

left.title: Low-Risk Criteria

Observation after R0 surgery without adjuvant TKI

right.title: High-Risk Criteria
points: Tumour size > 10 cm regardless of site
Tumour rupture before or during surgery

steps.tx: Succinate dehydrogenase-deficient **SDH-deficient GIST** arises in young patients and characteristically lacks KIT or PDGFRA kinase mutations. Arising in familial Carney-Stratakis syndrome or non-hereditary **Carney triad**, tumours present with multinodular gastric involvement, prominent lymph node metastases, and immunohistochemical loss of **SDHB** expression, displaying inherent clinical resistance to standard imatinib therapy.
